https://www.cei.int/ansa/178229.text: The Latvian Prosecutor's Office Launches an Investigation into AirBaltic's Finances (ANSA) - VILNIUS, JUL 25 - The Latvian Prosecutor General's Office has launched an investigation to determine whether AirBaltic's financial management complies with legal requirements. According to the announcement, the investigation was launched at the request of Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs to assess the company's management and shed light on the possible causes of the airline's crisis. Another investigation into AirBaltic's financial management had already been launched at the end of 2024, but no irregularities were found. AirBaltic is facing a particularly critical situation after two consecutive years of operating at a loss and the difficulty of finding investors willing to take over the company. (ANSA). https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cy4z.text: Figure caption, Watch: JD Vance "extremely sceptical" over alleged strike on Iranian wedding By Dan Sales Published 3 hours ago The US military is investigating Iranian claims that its strikes killed at least four people including two children at a wedding in southern Iran, Vice-President JD Vance has said. The Iranian Red Crescent Society (IRCS) - a humanitarian group - said shrapnel from a missile hit the ceremony at a home in Sirik on Tuesday, prompting Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei to declare it a "war crime". US missiles were fired the same day over "attempted attacks" by Iran on American forces, but a US Central Command spokesperson said it "never targets civilians". Speaking on Thursday, Vance said he was "extremely sceptical" over reports of the alleged strike but confirmed the US would investigate. Iran says US strike killed four at wedding in 'war crime' as US denies targeting civilians Published 1 day ago "I will say that the Iranian state media has not been a very good scribe about what's happened in the conflict thus far. So I'm extremely sceptical of this," Vance told a White House briefing. "I know that we're investigating." Iran has launched fresh attacks on US bases in Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates in response to the alleged strike. The IRCS said 67 people were hurt when shrapnel from the missile hit a family wedding ceremony, killing at least four people. Iranian state media said a fifth person, a woman aged 22, had died in hospital shortly after. The four people killed were named locally as Zarkhatoon Taheri, 50; Kolsum Mallahi Nazhdnia, 43; Mohammad Mallahi, 16; and Amirali Karimi, four. Image source, Iranian Red Crescent Society Image caption, A picture distributed by the Iranian Red Crescent Society purportedly showing the remains of a building which was hosting the wedding ceremony BBC Verify confirmed a video and two images taken on Tuesday near Kuhestak's coast that showed a telecommunications tower being destroyed, and other videos from Tuesday and Wednesday showed severely damaged houses about 130m (427ft) north of the tower. BBC Persian Forensics found the telecommunications tower was about 112m (367 ft) from the house where the wedding was being held. Fighting with Iran has continued for over half a year since the US and Israel launched a joint attack on the country on 28 February. https://www.bursa.ro/new-salary-law-cont.text: The draft salary law is generating dissatisfaction in several budgetary sectors. The Federation "Solidaritatea Sanitara" has launched a national consultation among employees in Health, while the National Federation of Trade Unions in Culture and Press CulturMedia is asking political parties not to vote for the project in its current form and is warning of a possible social conflict. The unions are complaining about both risks regarding income and the lack of consultation in the process of drafting certain provisions. *"Solidaritatea Sanitara" consults 60,000 employees The Federation "Solidaritatea Sanitara" has launched a public consultation at national level to find out the position of employees in Health regarding the draft salary law. Employees are invited to check, through the Health Salary Comparator, the income that would result from the application of the project and compare it with the salaries currently being paid. The tool has been updated with the provisions of the project in the form of August 20, 2026. Subsequently, each employee can fill out the consultation form, indicating whether the project would cause a decrease, an increase or the maintenance of current income. According to the federation, the invitation was sent directly, via SMS and e-mail, to approximately 60,000 Health employees, as well as through the organization's online communication channels. The final results are to be sent to political parties, in order to provide them with information on the impact of the project on employees in the system. The collective management bodies of the "Health Solidarity" Federation will establish the final position on the project based on the results of the consultation. *Modification of bonuses In parallel, the "Health Solidarity" Federation is carrying out an action to convince parliamentarians to modify some provisions. Among the demands are the exemption of units subordinated to the Ministry of Health from the 20% limit for bonuses and the introduction of a 30% ceiling. The Federation also requests a range of 50%-100% for additional hourly rates for work performed on days off and public holidays, as well as ensuring the financing of all salary influences resulting from the application of the new legislation. *CulturMedia demands the rejection of the project The dissatisfaction also extends to the Culture sector. The National Federation of Culture and Press Unions CulturMedia calls on political parties not to vote for the draft law on salaries in its current form and warns of a possible "large-scale" social conflict. According to the federation, the current form of the project does not eliminate inequities in the museum sector, but rather consolidates them and transforms them into state salary policy. CulturMedia claims that, on August 12, discussions took place regarding the salaries of museum staff without the representative trade union organizations being informed, invited or consulted. "The professional and salary future of the approximately 7,500 employees in Romanian museums cannot be decided through negotiations held in the absence of social partners,” states the federation. Trade unionists believe that the exclusion of representative organizations is incompatible with a real social dialogue, and the selective consultation of some representatives of the system cannot replace institutional negotiations with trade union organizations. The federation calls on the Ministry of Labor and the Ministry of Culture to publish the list of participants in the discussions of August 12, the mandate under which they formulated proposals for the museum sector, the minutes of the meetings, the resulting documents and the criteria that formed the basis of the current salary scales. CulturMedia also disputes the salary differences between positions in museums and those in performance and concert institutions. According to the federation's calculations, the coefficients of management positions in museums have been equalized with those in performance and concert institutions, while execution positions have lagged behind. The difference between the salary of a manager and that of an AI specialist, at the maximum salary level, would reach, according to the federation, 11,200 lei gross in museums, compared to 7,520 lei gross in performance and concert institutions. At the same time, an AI specialist in a museum would earn 3,680 lei gross less than an equivalent level specialist in a performance institution, claims CulturMedia. The federation also considers it unacceptable that a specialist in a large museum, with over 30 years of experience, an AI professional degree, maximum gradation and exceptional professional performance, should have a lower salary than a novice teacher in secondary education. *The reference value, another point of contention Another contested element is the reduction of the reference value from 4,325 to 4,000 lei. According to CulturMedia calculations, that This change leads to a loss of approximately 300 lei in salary, compared to the draft version presented in May. The Federation emphasizes that the salary must take into account the responsibility of specialists working in museum institutions and their role in preserving heritage. "Heritage is not researched, conserved, restored and transmitted to future generations by itself,” states CulturMedia, listing museographers, researchers, conservators, restorers, archaeologists, museum educators, supervisors and technical and administrative staff among the employees involved. CulturMedia warns that, in the event of the adoption of the draft without correcting the claimed inequities, it will use all legal means of union action and will notify the European Commission and other competent European institutions. The Federation argues that the Government and Parliament must assume the possible social consequences and blockages that could occur in the museum system. In this context, CulturMedia states that even events organized outside of working hours could be affected by employee dissatisfaction and invites managers favored by the new pay scales to organize such events themselves, including the Night of Museums in Villages, scheduled for August 29. The contestation of the salary project by the unions in Health, Culture and Press thus indicates that the debate on the new salary scale goes beyond the issue of income levels and includes topics such as financing, differences between professional categories and compliance with social dialogue mechanisms. https://www.politico.eu/article/european.text: NEW YORK — The president of the European Parliament, Roberta Metsola, says Germany should seek a deal with the Trump administration to resolve their trade dispute over drug pricing. “If you don’t talk directly and reach a deal — the art of the deal — then the consequences might be more difficult to swallow. So my advice to anyone would be: Just try to find it,” she said in an exclusive interview with POLITICO on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative is currently investigating Germany’s drug pricing policies, accusing it of “persistent underpayment” for pharmaceutical products. Advertisement Advertisement In a hearing this week in Washington, a clear majority of witnesses supported this claim. The investigation could ultimately provide the legal justification for Trump to impose new tariffs on German exports. Metsola advocated for a compromise between Washington and Berlin to avoid “an impossible race on drugs.” Europe could “still lead in pharmaceuticals,” she said. But the bloc has to become “much more agile, not only in pricing but also in terms of clinical trials and bringing new products on the market.” The center-right European People's Party politician, a member of the EU Parliament since 2013, serves in a role akin to that of the Speaker of the House in the U.S. A deal is a deal While Metsola backed negotiations over confrontation with the Trump White House, she also sent a clear warning to the U.S. government, suggesting any tariff increase on German goods would potentially violate the 15% tariff ceiling agreed in the deal that President Donald Trump struck with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen at his golf resort in Turnberry, Scotland, last year. Metsola pointed to a suspension clause the European Parliament had forced into the trade deal, warning that “there are legal consequences” if the Trump administration targets individual EU countries. “The agreement we voted on already foresaw that,” she said. She repeated this warning regarding U.S. tariffs on steel and aluminum derivatives. Under the Turnberry agreement, the U.S. must bring its high steel and aluminum derivative tariffs into line with a 15% tariff ceiling agreed to in Turnberry by the end of the year. Non-compliance by the U.S. side “would be a trigger alert” for the suspension clause, Metsola said. Advertisement Advertisement Digital sovereignty In a speech on the sidelines of the assembly on Tuesday, the Maltese politician called for “guardrails” for artificial intelligence, a hot-button issue in Washington at the moment after leaders of top American AI firms called for a slowdown in development of some of the most cutting-edge technologies. Asked if regulating AI risked Europe losing the competition against the U.S. and China, Metsola said: “I remain convinced that the race is not between the EU and the U.S. It is between democratic AI and autocratic AI. The EU and America have to be together in this race.” At the same time, Metsola rejected doubts about the bloc’s digital sovereignty. “We depend on U.S. tech. But U.S. tech depends on the EU market. This is what I think we don’t have in the conversation when tech leaders come to Europe and say: ‘We want to have a common market.’” The European Parliament in Strasbourg, France is pictured on Nov. 24, 2025. | Alexis Haulot/EP European lawmakers from across the political spectrum are currently pushing to extend the EU’s cornerstone AI Act to cover liability for U.S. tech giants whose cutting-edge models threaten global safety. Metsola seemed to support this initiative. “We should listen to the leaders of those AI models that themselves are saying to be careful and they themselves are calling for guardrails.” She pointed to the EU’s Digital Services Act as a potential “platform” for a future liability mechanism. Triangular trade While China’s President Xi meets with Trump in Washington this week, EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič is about to head to China . By mid-October, the bloc wants to reach an agreement with Beijing for better market access for European companies, Chinese government action on trade imbalances and overcapacity and greater certainty on critical raw materials. “We cannot afford to become a continent that is just a consumer continent,” Metsola insisted regarding EU-China relations. The EU needs an “honest,” “strong” and “self-confident” conversation with Beijing, she said. Advertisement Advertisement Metsola said the bloc had taken a similarly strong and self-confident stance in the crisis around Trump’s threats to annex Greenland at the beginning of 2026, and also when von der Leyen last week invited Canada to become an associate member . But despite strong ties with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and his country, crucial elements of bilateral agreements are still in limbo. Metsola called on the 10 remaining EU countries that have not ratified the decade-old CETA free-trade deal between the European Union and Canada to finally do so. The leaders of the EU and Canada are expected to hold a summit in Montreal in October, where both sides are aiming to seal a Digital Trade Agreement. Metsola dismissed concerns over the absence of dedicated AI provisions. “The idea of having separate chapters on AI would be akin to having chapters on the internet in the past,” she said, arguing that the technology will permeate every aspect of economic activity. Recently, Metsola’s center-right EPP has repeatedly relied on support from right-wing groups to pass legislation, drawing sharp criticism from Socialists and Greens. Metsola declined to give a direct answer when asked whether she wanted the EPP to rule out future alliances with hard-right parties such as Germany’s AfD and France’s Rassemblement National. “I am a proper centrist,” she said. “I have always believed that majorities should be built from the center outwards. That gives you a stronger mandate when negotiating with the Council.” There would be votes in the future “that will depend on different majorities,” she added. “I’m the president, I represent all the members. I just want predictability and stability.” At the beginning of 2027, Metsola is expected to run for a third consecutive term as president of the European Parliament, but she did not confirm this to POLITICO. Asked if she had any ambitions to eventually run for president of the European Commission, Metsola said: “It is the honor of a lifetime and the responsibility of a lifetime to run this parliament. It’s not easy. So I focus on that.”
